items.title: Percy Stovall Interview, 1977-12-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I remember it's five years, right Ponce? Right.

ctx.x: No, it had to be in his 60s, I believe. It had to be, it could have been 59 into the 60s, I'm just guessing now. But he got a divorce from his wife in Chicago around, probably around 56 or 57, I believe. And then he, they buy the property up, he got the money, he met this woman here. They stayed together for maybe 3 or 4 or 5, I don't know. So then he went to California, in fact he called me once in a while, he's met again in California. You get a lot of wicked to them overseas, they put the old package together,…

They always do. They always do. I can dance on. I can dance on. I remember it's five years, right Ponce? Right. This must have been, the transition to the music of the 50s must have been different for you in a way, because you're coming from your time period. But when you were a young man, what would the records that were popular?

Well, even when I was young, the popular record was Duke Ellison, Count Basie, Fletcher Henderson, and all those kind of things, 10, 15 piece bands, you know. And then Lewis Jordan came along and brought it down to the five pieces, didn't they've been going down there, essentially. Then Fess Domino and Evelyn Presser came out with the rock and roll deal, but that changed the trend from the big band altogether, you see. But no, it didn't make any difference. All I did, each year, I mean the trend changed, the…
